question: Which statement best describes Main idea?
options: Check an optional property before calling a method or using it as a definite value. For example, test `if (user.name)` when an empty name also counts as absent, or check `user.name !== undefined` when empty text is valid. It is like checking whether a form answer was filled in before reading it. For example, check `name !== undefined` when an empty string is still a valid value.

`readonly id: string` prevents code using that type from assigning a new value to `id`. It is like printing an ID on a badge that should not be edited. This is a compile-time rule. Other code or JavaScript can still change the object unless runtime protections are added. For example, mark a creation timestamp readonly when callers should not replace it.

`name?: string` means an object may have a string `name` property or may omit it. It is like an optional question on a form. Code should check that the value exists before using string methods. Use optional fields when absence has a clear meaning, rather than making every field optional for convenience. For example, a profile can omit a nickname while requiring an account ID.

Readonly is shallow unless applied to nested property types as well. A readonly property that points to an object does not automatically freeze the object inside. It is like protecting a folder label while leaving its papers editable. Use immutable data patterns or runtime freezing when the application needs deeper protection. For example, a readonly object property can still point to a mutable nested array.
explanation: `name?: string` means an object may have a string `name` property or may omit it. It is like an optional question on a form. Code should check that the value exists before using string methods. Use optional fields when absence has a clear meaning, rather than making every field optional for convenience. For example, a profile can omit a nickname while requiring an account ID.
